tests: A three-page bundle where pages 1 and 3 have a text layer and page 2 is a scanned image with none.
attacks: Whole-document OCR decisions. A pipeline that asks 'is this document scanned?' gets the wrong answer either way: skip OCR and page 2 is lost, force OCR and pages 1 and 3 get re-recognised text over a perfectly good text layer — which replaces correct characters with OCR guesses and is an assertion failure.
generation: Pages 1 and 3 render natively from h14-mixed-scan.html; page 2 renders from h14-mixed-scan.scan.html to PNG, becomes a one-page PDF via `pdfbox fromimage`, and the three are assembled with `pdfbox split` and `pdfbox merge`.
title: Lease File Bundle
headingHierarchyNote: Page 2's 'PORT AUTHORITY · WESTERN QUAY' is visually a heading but is inside the scan. It only becomes recoverable after OCR, and is excluded from the expected sequence above because a non-OCR run cannot be faulted for missing it.

figures.expectedHandling: OCR to a text layer, then normal tagging. Describing the page as a figure with alt text is wrong — it is a page of text, not an image of a thing.

expectedOutcome: Correct results are OCR applied to page 2 only, or NEEDS_REVIEW naming page 2 as un-recovered. Applying OCR to pages 1 and 3 is an assertion failure even if the recognised text happens to be close.
intentionalProblems: mixed text-layer and image-only pages in one document
